unconnected.label: Aquarium equipment · protected feed proposal NOT energized
Aquarium lateral dry-bay cassette · fixed feed proposed, NOT energized

review: The source already has a generic internal filter casing. It is retained and given a visible power lead, not duplicated. Heater, LED bar and battery food dispenser are additional generic proposals, not selected products.
Three real flex runs plug into a NEW proposed four-outlet dry service panel; one outlet is spare. This is not a multi-plug adapter in the old blank cover.

Flush timber skins wrap the existing metal stand without altering its frame or tank support. The adjacent low dry bay is wholly outside the tank footprint, separated by a side wall; there is no mains panel under the water. Lift-off front and upper/lower shadow gaps give access and airflow, not an IP certification.

Separate shallow rear trough has a lift-off cap and slotted face; cables remain accessible without lifting the wet lid or cutting plugs. No sealed cable bundle, shared aquarium/mains tray or wet-location extension is introduced.

A protected surface-feed proposal now connects the low connection reservation to the dry service panel, avoiding the accessible isolation control. This is NOT energized: DB/circuit, isolation wiring, earth continuity and protective devices are not designed or verified.

Panel is a compact east-facing two-by-two outlet cassette wholly west of x=.94, not a front-facing plate trapped behind the mandir. Remove the first tank-stand front skin and service it laterally through the clear gap between the retained frame legs. The shared side is intentionally open; the cassette has a solid rear mounting partition. Kneeling reach and supplier backbox/plug fit still require a mockup. No tank lifting or mandir movement.

The side bay is outside the tank's vertical leak footprint, but a real floor-level leak or splash can still reach it. Site splash/flood exposure, dedicated protection, accessible isolation, sealed backbox choice and a reach/removal mockup are mandatory approval gates before energizing.

All three equipment leads show drip-loop intent and over-rim entry. The lower bay requires longer factory-supplied flex, especially at the heater; select and verify actual lead lengths against these routes or revise the design. Do not splice, extend or add wet-location extension cords to make the illustration fit.

The revised editable lid now has two cable notches and a separate feeder opening. Smooth edge trims and cable support are illustrated. Actual lid material, feeding clearance, humidity protection, cleaning/lift-off access and fabrication require supplier approval.
The automatic food dispenser is a battery-operated proposal: it deliberately has no mains cord. Battery checks, moisture protection and a trial of feed quantities are required before relying on it.

Filter outlet implies circulation, not verified oxygenation. Stocking, filtration duty, heater need/wattage, light schedule and any separate aerator must be selected for the livestock, tank volume and ambient conditions.

Water level and rim geometry are unchanged. Heater is below the current water surface; feeding drop and light placement are only illustrative. No filled tank/support, electrical or aquatic-life safety certification.
Conventional 5.1: five passive speakers are driven by the receiver; they do not each need a mains socket. The active subwoofer has both a dedicated power lead and a separate LFE signal.

Generic compact receiver sits on the console top, not inside the shallow closed cupboard. Its top remains open and its rear has a nominal 90mm cable zone. Select a unit that actually fits; manufacturer ventilation/connector space overrides these provisional dimensions.

Front speaker and HDMI cables use physically cut rear channels and local ports in the timber backing. The front face is uninterrupted: no applied horizontal raceway across the design. Lift-off joinery access is a fabrication proposal, not a structural wall chase.

Rear speaker pairs use physically grooved, removable paint-matched nonstructural lining: an upper east service band, north high-level return and west lining below the AC, with local ports behind speakers. No applied white tube crosses the finished wall, no loose floor lead, and no structural wall/beam chase is implied. Lining fixings, substrate, fire/cable class and fabrication need site coordination.

Mains-only outlets for receiver/subwoofer and NVR/PoE are separate from passive signal paths. Existing ONT/router backup preference is retained without extending it to NVR/PoE. No shared unpartitioned mains/data raceway or extension strip.

Receiver-to-TV HDMI eARC, set-top and NVR HDMI, ONT/router/PoE/NVR patch leads are physical proposals. Camera home runs, ISP entry, impedance, polarity, cable class, bend limits and calibration remain selected-product/site work.
Speaker locations are retained, not acoustically certified. Commission levels, crossover, delays and subwoofer position by listening/measurement at the actual seating.

Network bay uses actual concealed underside intake and high rear openings, keeping the timber door face uncut. They provide a passive airflow proposal, not a verified thermal calculation. Check equipment dissipation and temperature with the door closed; add suitable quiet ventilation or relocate if the selected products require it.

limits: Solid 3D flex and plugs are physical-layout proposals, not dashed control links or building wiring.

Cable diameters, plug/adapter shapes and drawn lengths illustrate appearance only; no electrical rating or supplied lead length is selected.

Unused sockets remain empty. Aquarium fixed-feed containment is proposed, NOT energized. Neither it nor conditional AC/geyser leads prove a designed/tested building circuit.
